definition: Triumphant means feeling or showing exultant joy over a victory or success — the win, worn openly.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word triumphant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know triumphant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Nadia's triumphant shout carried across the pool deck the instant the scoreboard confirmed her record.
Pleased is weaker than triumphant: a pleased winner smiles quietly to herself, while a triumphant one lets the joy of victory pour out for everyone to see.
Gloating goes further than triumphant — and turns sour: triumphant joy simply overflows, but gloating aims that joy at the loser to rub the defeat in.

Victorious states a fact about the outcome: you won. Triumphant describes the joy that follows and shows — a team can be victorious on paper while only the player hoisting the trophy and beaming looks triumphant.
Jubilant means loudly, openly joyful about anything — a jubilant crowd may simply be glad it's Friday. Triumphant ties that joy to a win: it is jubilation with a victory behind it.

Triumphant needs two ingredients: a victory behind the feeling and joy out where people can see it.

That keeps it distinct from victorious, which only reports the result, and from this unit's ecstatic, which is overwhelming delight from any cause at all — a lottery winner is ecstatic, not triumphant, because nothing was contested.
And when the display starts targeting the loser, the honest word is no longer triumphant but gloating.
